newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips, banks await C.Bank stance.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips, banks await C.Bank stance.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower in dull trade confined to slight commercial and short covering, dealers said.
Banks were not willing to build positions despite low call rates, as they were not sure if the Central Bank would remain bullish towards the dollar, they said.
The rupee closed at 57.73 to the dollar after opening at 57.66. The currency closed at 57.70 on Tuesday.
"Apart from a little import and short covering, movement was ranged because no one wants to build positions though call rates were low," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
Though the Central Bank had been bullish and pushed up the dollar middle rate by 48.75 local cents in January, banks were waiting to see how it would react in February, he said.
Overnight call money closed at 12.25, with the markt well offered.
Dealers said the money market was very liquid, and saw no reason for rates to rise in the near-term.
Treasury Bill yields continued to slide at Wednesday's auction which was heavily oversubscribed.
Bids received amounted to 7.8 billion rupees with only 3.1 billion worth accepted.
